examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Cartesian Equation of Parabola Given Its Parametric Equations
examples.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x-1 = -2t^2, \qquad y+1 = -4t, \qquad t\in(-\infty, \infty).
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-\frac{x-1}{2},\,t=-\frac{y+1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(-\frac{y+1}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation $t^2 = -\dfrac{x-1}{2}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16} & =-\frac{x-1}{2} \\ (y+1)^{2} & =16\cdot (-\frac{x-1}{2}) \\ (y+1)^{2} & =-8(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation $(y-2)^{2}=16(x+6)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h)$ that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case $(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),$ we see that the parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-6,2).$ So we have

$$
x+6=p{t}^{2},\,y-2=2pt.
$$

Now, comparing the right-hand sides of the given Cartesian equation and the general case, then solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4p(x-h) & =16(x+6) \\ 4p(x+6) & =16(x+6) \\ 4p & =16 \\ p & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+6=(4){t}^{2},\,y-2=2(4)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+6=4{t}^{2},\,y-2=8t.
$$
